read_board · record_assessment · VERDICT: cite · draft_verdict

p.i:
Each seat reads only its own assessments and its own draft.
That one is an app-side filter inside read_board, NOT the browser.
The origin partition above it is the browser's.

ADVOCATE A · theboard-a · ADVOCATE B · theboard-b
iframe allow=tools

div.style: color: rgb(169, 162, 156) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.i:
Three ways a panel gets its moves: a fixed script in the page with
no model at all, this project's own model proxy, or your agent over
the bridge. The tool boundary is identical in all three.

span.p: theboard-record.netlify.app · owns the case, and nothing else

span.p:
The case file
exhibits · facts · disputes · objections · assessments · verdicts

div.style: color: rgb(243, 242, 242) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Phase machine · FILING → REVIEW → VERDICT → CONFIRMED
spend_appeal sends VERDICT back to REVIEW, once per side

div.style: color: rgb(243, 242, 242) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Ledger tape
every executeTool from any frame below lands here
by origin, ok or refused. A call for a tool the frame never
held is refused before it arrives, so it leaves no row.

div.style: color: rgb(243, 242, 242) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Tool registry · registerTool spec, signal, exposedTo
one AbortController per lifetime
abort is withdrawal: WebMCP has no unregisterTool.
A phase change aborts lifetimes. So does spending an appeal,
which is an abort with no phase change behind it.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: Outside the browser · a judge brings their own agent

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(243, 242, 242) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Claude Code, or Codex
you supply it. This project never runs it.

div.style: color: rgb(243, 242, 242) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
external-agent bridge
an MCP server, no provider key
MCP over stdio: tools/list · tools/call

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

p.i:
Each frame asks getTools fromOrigins. The BROWSER answers it,
against exposedTo on the site's own registration.
Not this application, which never sees the question.

div.style: color: rgb(243, 242, 242) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Any visiting agent · Chrome's own, an extension, anything
read_board only, read-only, and it sees the WHOLE board.
Registered with NO origin named. Deliberate, and disclosed.
Its reads land on the tape like everyone else's.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
confirm · return_with_note · never registered to any origin, in any phase
not withheld, not refused. Never written down.
Writes the outcome straight to the case, not through a tool, so it leaves no tape row either.
